Know that in His saying ﴿Dhikr [a reminder]﴾ there are two interpretations.

The first: Exalted is He only mentioned the circumstances of these prophets, peace be upon them, so that Muhammad, peace be upon him, would endure the folly of his people with patience. When He had completed the explanation of this path and wished to mention, after it, another path that requires patience in the face of the folly of the ignorant, and wished to distinguish one of the two sections from the other, He said, without doubt, ﴿This is a reminder﴾. Then He began to establish the second section, saying ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing [muttaqin]﴾. This is like an author who, having completed a passage, says "This is a section," then begins another section. And when a writer finishes a chapter of his book and wishes to begin another, he says: "This is what was, and such-and-such." The proof of this is that when He completed the mention of the people of Paradise and wished to follow it with the mention of the people of Hell, He said: ﴿This, and indeed for the rebellious there is an evil return﴾ [Sad: 55].

The second interpretation: what is meant is that this is an honour and a good remembrance for these prophets, peace be upon them, by which they will be mentioned forever. The first is the correct one.

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good return﴾.

Know that when Exalted is He related about the disbelievers of Quraysh their folly toward the Prophet ﷺ, in that they described him as a sorcerer and a liar, and said to him in mockery, ﴿Our Lord, hasten to us our portion [of punishment]﴾, at this point He commanded Muhammad to be patient with that folly, and He made clear that this patience is obligatory for two reasons:

The first: Exalted is He, having shown that the earlier prophets endured hardships and afflictions with patience, it is obligatory for you to follow them in this matter.

The second: Exalted is He, in this verse, made clear that whoever obeys God will have such-and-such reward, and whoever disobeys Him will have such-and-such punishment, and all of this requires patience in observing the obligations of God, Exalted is He. This is a fine arrangement and a subtle sequence.

As for the saying of Exalted is He, ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good return﴾: al-ma'ab means the place of return. Those who hold the view of the eternity of souls [qidam al-arwah] have used this verse as evidence, and every verse that contains the word "return" (rujū'). The basis of their argument is that the word "return" applies only if these souls existed before the bodies and were in the presence of God's majesty, and then became attached to the bodies; so when they are separated from the bodies, that is called a return. The answer to this is: if it indicates anything, it indicates only that souls existed before bodies, and it does not indicate the eternity of souls.

* * *

Then Exalted is He said: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, which is a substitution [badal] for His saying ﴿a good return﴾. Then He said: ﴿with gates opened for them﴾. In this there are several issues:

Issue one: They have mentioned several interpretations of this expression:

The first: al-Farra' said: its meaning is "with its gates opened for them." The Arabs use the definite article (al-alif wa-l-lam) as a replacement for the possessive construction (idafa). The Arabs say: "I passed by a man whose face is good [hasan al-wajh]," so the al- in al-wajh is a substitute for the possessive.

The second: al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "with its gates opened for them" from it.

The third: the author of al-Kashshaf [al-Zamakhshari] said: ﴿al-abwab [the gates]﴾ is a substitution [badal] for the pronoun, and its implied sense is: "opened, they, the gates," like your saying "Zayd struck the hand and the foot," and this is badal al-ishtimal [substitution of inclusion/comprehension].

Issue two: It was read: "Gardens of Eden, opened" in the nominative, on the basis that the phrase ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾ is the subject [mubtada'] and "opened" is its predicate [khabar], and both are the predicate of an omitted subject, that is: "it is ﴿Gardens of Eden, opened for them﴾."

Issue three: Know that Exalted is He described, in this verse, several aspects of the state of the people of Paradise:

The first: the state of their dwellings. His saying ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾ indicates two matters:

One of them: that they are gardens and orchards.

The second: that they are lasting, safe from coming to an end.

As for His saying ﴿with gates opened for them﴾, there are several interpretations:

The first: that the meaning is that the angels assigned to the gardens, when they see the owner of the garden, open its gates for him and greet him with peace. Thus he enters, surrounded by the angels, in the most honoured state and most beautiful form. Exalted is He said: ﴿Until, when they come to it and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it to abide therein"﴾ [al-Zumar: 73].

The second: that whenever they wish those gates to open, they open for them, and whenever they wish them to close, they close for them.

The third: the purpose of this opening is to describe those dwellings as spacious, with the eyes wandering freely through them, and the witnessing of pleasant and delightful states.

* * *

Then Exalted is He said: ﴿Reclining therein, calling therein for [various] fruit and drink﴾. In this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: In this verse He mentioned their reclining in Paradise, and in other verses He mentioned the manner of that reclining. He said in one verse: ﴿reclining on couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56], and in another verse: ﴿reclining on green cushions [rafraf]﴾ [al-Rahman: 76].

The second discussion: His saying ﴿reclining therein﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) placed before its governing element, which is His saying ﴿calling therein﴾. The meaning is: they call in the Gardens, ﴿reclining therein﴾. Then He said: ﴿for abundant fruit and drink﴾, meaning: for varieties of fruit and varieties of drink; the implied sense is: for abundant fruit and abundant drink. The reason for mentioning this meaning is that the lands of the Arabs are hot and have few fruits and drinks, so God encouraged them toward it.

When Exalted is He had made clear the matter of the dwelling and the matter of food and drink, He mentioned after that the matter of marriage, saying: ﴿And with them are those who restrain their gaze [qasirat al-tarf]﴾. Its explanation has already been given in Surat al-Saffat. In sum, the meaning of "restraining their gaze" is that they do not look at others, and their hearts are confined to love for them. His saying ﴿of equal age [atrab]﴾ means of one age. It is possible that the maidens are of equal age, and it is possible that they are of equal age to their husbands. Al-Qaffal said: the reason for considering this attribute is that when they resemble one another in attribute, age, and adornment, inclination toward them is equal, and that requires the absence of jealousy.

* * *

Then Exalted is He informed about the permanence of the reward, saying: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end﴾.

﴿This. And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return.﴾ ﴿Hell, which they will burn in, so wretched is the resting place.﴾ ﴿This! So let them taste it: boiling water and dark, icy fluid.﴾ ﴿And other punishments of similar kind, in pairs.﴾ ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you. No welcome for them; indeed, they will burn in the Fire.﴾ ﴿They will say: "Rather, you! No welcome for you. You brought this upon us, so wretched is the abode."﴾ ﴿They will say: "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase for him a double punishment in the Fire."﴾ ﴿And they will say: "What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?﴾ ﴿Did we take them in mockery, or have our eyes failed to see them?"﴾ ﴿Indeed, that is true: the disputing of the people of the Fire.﴾

Allah, exalted is He, when He described the reward of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), afterwards described the punishment of the transgressors (al-taghun), so that the warning would be mentioned after the promise, and intimidation after encouragement.

Know that Allah, exalted is He, mentioned several aspects concerning the Fire:

The first is their place of return and their final destination. He said: ﴿This. And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return.﴾ This stands in contrast to His words: ﴿And indeed, for the God-fearing is a good place of return.﴾ Thus Allah clarified that the state of the transgressors is opposed to the state of the God-fearing. Scholars differed over who is meant by "the transgressors." Most exegetes understood it to refer to disbelievers. Al-Juba'i (al-Jubba'i) said that it refers to the people of major sins, whether they were disbelievers or not.

Those who held the first view argued with several points:

The first: His words ﴿an evil place of return﴾ imply that their return is worse than the return of others, and this applies only to disbelievers.

The second: Allah relates that they said: ﴿Did we take them in mockery?﴾ and this is fitting only for disbelievers, because a sinner does not take a believer as an object of mockery.

The third: it is a term of blame, and an unrestricted term is applied to its complete instance, and the complete instance of transgression is the disbeliever. Al-Juba'i supported his view with the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [Al-Alaq: 6–7], and this shows that the description of transgression may apply to one who commits a grave sin. Also, everyone who oversteps Allah's obligations and exceeds them has transgressed. Having understood this, we say: Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: the meaning is that those who transgressed and denied My messengers will have an evil place of return, that is, an evil destination and final abode. Then He said: ﴿Hell, which they will burn in.﴾ The meaning is that when Allah judged that the transgressors have an evil place of return, He explained it with His words: ﴿Hell, which they will burn in.﴾ Then He said: ﴿so wretched is the resting place﴾, similar to His words: ﴿They will have from Hell a bed, and over them coverings﴾ [Al-A'raf: 41]. Allah likened what lies beneath them of the Fire to the bed that a sleeper spreads out for himself.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿This! So let them taste it: boiling water and dark, icy fluid.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: there are two views:

The first: it is in inverted order, and the meaning is: "This is boiling water and dark fluid, so let them taste it."

The second: the meaning is: "Hell, which they will burn in, so wretched is the resting place. This! So let them taste it." Then it begins anew: "Boiling water and dark fluid."

[p. 193]

The second issue: *ghassaq* (dark, icy fluid), with or without the doubled letter, has several interpretations:

The first: it is that which flows from the pus of the people of the Fire. It is said: "the eye *ghasaqat*," when its tears flowed. Ibn Umar said: it is the pus that flows from them, which is gathered and given to them to drink.

The second: it was said that the boiling water burns by its heat, and the *ghassaq* burns by its cold. Al-Azhari mentioned that *ghasiq* means cold, and for this reason the night is called *ghasiq*, because it is colder than the day.

The third: that *ghassaq* means foul-smelling. Al-Zajjaj related: if a single drop of it were poured in the east, it would make the people of the west stink, and if a single drop of it were poured in the west, it would make the people of the east stink.

The fourth: Ka'b said: *ghassaq* is a spring in Hell into which flows the venom of every creature with a sting, such as scorpions and snakes.

The third issue: Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs, from Asim, read *ghassaq* with a doubled *sin* wherever it occurs, while the rest read it without doubling. Abu Ali al-Farisi said: the preferred reading is the single *sin*, because if it is doubled, it must be either a noun or an adjective. If it is a noun, nouns rarely come in this pattern; and if it is an adjective, it has been used in place of the noun it modifies, and the original rule is that this is not permitted.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And other punishments of similar kind, in pairs.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Amr read *wa-ukhar* with a *damma* on the *alif*, as the plural of *ukhra*, meaning "other kinds of punishment." This is also the reading of Mujahid. The rest read *akhar* in the singular, meaning "another punishment." On the first reading, His words *wa-ukhar* mean "and other things tasted, of similar kind to this tasted thing," that is, similar in severity and horror. *Azwaj* means "kinds." On the second reading, the implied meaning is "and another punishment or tasted thing," and *azwaj* is an adjective of *akhar*, because it may be a description of the kinds, or an adjective of the three: boiling water, dark fluid, and "another of similar kind." The author of *al-Kashshaf* (the commentary by al-Zamakhshari) said: it was recited *min shiklihi* with a kasra, which is a dialect form, whereas *al-Ghanj* (a plant term) is only with a kasra.

Having understood this: when Allah described the dwelling and the food of the transgressors, He related their condition with those who were their friends in this world first, and then with those who were their enemies in this world second.

As for the first, it is His words: ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you.﴾ Know that this is a quotation of the speech of the leaders of the people of the Fire, one saying it to another, as evidenced by what is quoted after this from the words of the followers: ﴿They will say: "Rather, you! No welcome for you. You brought this upon us."﴾ It has also been said that His words ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾ are the speech of the angelic guardians to the leaders of the disbelievers, about their followers, and His words ﴿No welcome for them; indeed, they will burn in the Fire﴾ are the speech of the leaders. His words ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾ mean: this is a dense multitude that has rushed into the Fire with you, just as they rushed with you into ignorance and error. The meaning of *iqtaham ma'akum al-nar* is that it entered the Fire in your company. *Iqtiham* means to plunge into hardship and enter it, and *qahma* means severe hardship.

His words ﴿No welcome for them﴾ are a curse from them upon their followers. A man says to one he wishes well: "Marhaban," meaning "You have come to a spacious land, not as a stranger," or "Your land is spacious." Then the particle *la* ("no") is placed before it in a curse. His words ﴿for them﴾ specify those upon whom the curse falls, and that "they will burn in the Fire" is the reason they deserve the curse. A parallel to this verse is His words: ﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [Al-A'raf: 38]. ﴿They will say﴾, that is, the followers: ﴿"Rather, you! No welcome for you"﴾, meaning that the curse you pronounced upon us, O leaders, is more deserved by you. They justified this with their words: ﴿"You brought this upon us."﴾ The pronoun refers to the punishment, or to their burning.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of their bringing the punishment upon them? We say: what makes it necessary to bring it forward is the doing of evil. Allah said: ﴿"Taste the punishment of burning." ﴿That is for what your hands have sent forth﴾ [Al-Anfal: 50–51]. Yet since the leaders were the cause of it through their misleading, and the punishment was their recompense for it, it was said: "You brought this upon us." Thus the leaders were made the ones who sent it forward, and the recompense was made the thing sent forward. The pronoun in His words ﴿you brought it﴾ is an allusion to the transgression that is indicated by His words: ﴿And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil place of return,﴾ and His words ﴿so wretched is the resting place﴾, meaning: wretched is the abode and dwelling, Hell. Then the followers said: ﴿"Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase for him a double punishment"﴾, meaning multiplied, that is, one that has double. A parallel is His words: ﴿"Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 38]. Similarly, His words: ﴿"Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way." ﴿"Our Lord, give them double the punishment"﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 67–68].

If it is asked: every amount of punishment that is imposed, if it is according to what is deserved, it will not be multiplied; and if it exceeds that, it is injustice, and that is not permitted. We say: what is meant is His words, peace be upon him (ﷺ): "Whoever initiates an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of those who act upon it until the Day of Resurrection." The meaning is that one of the two portions is the punishment for going astray, and the second is the punishment for leading others astray. And Allah knows best.

Here ends the explanation of the states of the disbelievers with those who were their beloved friends in this world. As for the explanation of their states with those who were their enemies in this world, it is His words: ﴿And they will say: "What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?"﴾ He means that when the disbelievers look toward the sides of Hell, they will then say: ﴿"What is wrong with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?"﴾ They mean the poor Muslims whom they did not regard, and whom they called "the wicked," either in the sense of the base, who had no good in them and no benefit, or because they were opposed to their religion and therefore considered wicked by them. Then they said: ﴿"Did we take them in mockery?"﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: Abu Amr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read *(min al-ashrar ittakhadhnahum)* with a connected *alif* on *ittakhadhnahum*, while the rest read it with a hamzated *alif* as an interrogative. Abu Ubayd said: it is read with the connected form, because the interrogative has already occurred in His words ﴿What is wrong with us that we do not see men﴾, and because the polytheists do not doubt that they took the believers in the world as objects of mockery, since Allah has informed about this in His words: ﴿But you took them in mockery, until they made you forget My remembrance﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 110]. So how is it fitting to ask about something they know? Al-Farra' answered this by saying: this is one of the interrogatives whose meaning is wonder and reproach, and such an interrogative about a known matter is permissible. As for the view of those who attached the hamza as an interrogative, it is that it must be taken this way so that it balances His words ﴿Did we take them?﴾ with *am* in His words ﴿Or have our eyes failed to see them?﴾. If it is asked: what is the balancing clause for His words ﴿Or have our eyes failed?﴾ on the first reading? We say: it is omitted, and the meaning is: "Are they the ones we sought, or have our eyes failed to see them?"

The second issue: Nafi' read *sukhriyyan* with a *damma* on the *sin*, while the rest read it with a *kasra*. It has been said that both have the same meaning. It has also been said that with the *kasra* it means mockery, and with the *damma* it means subjugation and making subservient.

The third issue: they differed on the structure of the verse according to the two readings mentioned. As for the reading as a statement, the meaning is: "What is wrong with us that we do not see them present, because of their insignificance they were left behind, or because our eyes have failed to see them?" Their insignificance is expressed by their words ﴿Did we take them in mockery?﴾ As for the reading as an interrogative, the meaning is: "Is it because we have taken them as objects of mockery, and they are not such, so they did not enter the Fire? Or is it because our eyes have failed to see them?"

Know that when Allah related this debate of theirs, He said: "Indeed, that which We have related of them is true, and they must speak of it." Then He explained what it was that We related of them, and said: ﴿the disputing of the people of the Fire.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, called those words "disputing" because the leaders' words ﴿No welcome for them﴾ and the followers' words ﴿Rather, you! No welcome for you﴾ are of the nature of contention.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 38, verses 65–70:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I am only a warner, and there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ ﴿Say: It is a great tidings.﴾ ﴿You are turning away from it.﴾ ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed.﴾ ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner.﴾

Know that when, at the beginning of the surah, He related that Muhammad (ﷺ), when he invited people to the belief that there is no god but one God, and that he is a clear messenger from Allah, and that the claim of the Resurrection is true, those disbelievers displayed foolishness, said that he is a sorcerer and a liar, and mocked his words. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the stories of the prophets for two reasons:

The first: so that this would move Muhammad (ﷺ) to follow the example of the prophets, peace be upon them, in patience over the folly of the people.

The second: so that this would deter the disbelievers from persisting in disbelief and foolishness, and would call them to accept faith. When Allah, exalted is He, completed this path, He followed it with another path, which is the description of the bliss of the people of reward and the description of the punishment of the people of punishment. When Allah, exalted is He, completed these clarifications, He returned to affirming the matters mentioned at the beginning of the surah, which are the affirmation of tawhid, prophethood and resurrection. So He said: Say, O Muhammad, I am only a warner, and there is no escape from acknowledging that there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer. For the correct order is that we first mention the doubts of the opponents and answer them, then after them we mention the proofs that indicate the soundness of the matter sought. Likewise here, Allah, exalted is He, answered their doubt and drew attention to the corruption of their words, then after it He mentioned what indicates the soundness of these matters, because removing what is not fitting precedes establishing what is fitting, and cleaning a slate of corrupt inscriptions precedes writing correct inscriptions upon it. Whoever considers this order will acknowledge that the discourse from the beginning of the surah to its end has come in the best of arrangements and composition.

As for His saying: ﴿Say: I am only a warner﴾, meaning: I convey the states of punishment for whoever denies tawhid, prophethood and the return, and the states of reward for whoever affirms them. Know that when, at the beginning of the surah, He related that Muhammad (ﷺ), when he invited people to the belief that there is no god but one God, and that he is a clear messenger from Allah, and that the claim of the Resurrection is true, those disbelievers displayed foolishness, said that he is a sorcerer and a liar, and mocked his words. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the stories of the prophets for two reasons:

The first: so that this would move Muhammad (ﷺ) to follow the example of the prophets, peace be upon them, in patience over the folly of the people.

The second: so that this would deter the disbelievers from persisting in disbelief and foolishness, and would call them to accept faith. When Allah, exalted is He, completed this path, He followed it with another path, which is the description of the bliss of the people of reward and the description of the punishment of the people of punishment. When Allah, exalted is He, completed these clarifications, He returned to affirming the matters mentioned at the beginning of the surah, which are the affirmation of tawhid, prophethood and resurrection. So He said: Say, O Muhammad, I am only a warner, and there is no escape from acknowledging that there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer. For the correct order is that we first mention the doubts of the opponents and answer them, then after them we mention the proofs that indicate the soundness of the matter sought. Likewise here, Allah, exalted is He, answered their doubt and drew attention to the corruption of their words, then after it He mentioned what indicates the soundness of these matters, because removing what is not fitting precedes establishing what is fitting, and cleaning a slate of corrupt inscriptions precedes writing correct inscriptions upon it. Whoever considers this order will acknowledge that the discourse from the beginning of the surah to its end has come in the best of arrangements and composition.

As for His saying: ﴿Say: I am only a warner﴾, meaning: I convey the states of punishment for whoever denies tawhid, prophethood and the return, and the states of reward for whoever affirms them. And just as He began at the beginning of the surah with the proofs of tawhid, where He related of them that they said ﴿Has he made the gods one God?﴾, so here He began with the affirmation of tawhid, saying: ﴿There is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ In this statement there is an indication of the proof that He is exalted above partner and equal. Its explanation: whatever is made a partner with Him in divinity either exists as one capable absolutely of disposing of the world, or it does not, but is rather an inanimate, powerless thing.

The first is invalid, because if His partner were absolutely capable, He would not be capable and subduing, since, supposing He wills something and His partner wills the opposite of that thing, neither of the two outcomes would be more fitting than the other, which leads to each of them canceling the other; then He would not be capable and subduing, but rather weak and powerless, and the powerless is not fit for divinity. So His saying ﴿but Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ indicates that His being Subduer shows that He is One.

As for the second, namely that what is made a partner with Him has no power at all, like these idols, this too is invalid, because plain reason judges that worship of the capable, subduing God is more fitting than worship of an inanimate thing that does not hear, does not see, and does not avail you anything. So His saying ﴿There is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ indicates these proofs. Know that His being Subduer, glorified is He, conveys fear and warning, so when He mentioned that, He followed it with what indicates hope and encouragement, saying: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving.﴾ His being Lord conveys nurturing, kindness, generosity and bounty, and His being Forgiving conveys encouragement. This Being is the One whose worship is obligatory, because He is the One whose punishment is feared and whose grace and reward are hoped for.

We shall mention another way of explaining these verses. We say: He, exalted is He, mentioned five of His attributes in this place: the One, the Subduer, the Lord, the Mighty, and the Forgiving. As for His being One, it is the matter over which dispute arose between the people of truth and the polytheists, and He, exalted is He, proved His oneness by His being Subduer. We have already explained the manner of this indication, but although His being Subduer indicates the affirmation of oneness, it also necessitates intense fear, so He followed it with the mention of three attributes indicating mercy, grace and generosity.

The first of them: His being Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. Knowledge of this is only completed by considering the traces of Allah's wisdom in the creation of the heavens and the earth, the four elements and the three generated kinds, and that is a sea without shore. When you reflect on the traces of His wisdom and mercy in the creation of these things, you then know His nurturing of all, and that conveys great hope.

The second: His being Mighty. The benefit of mentioning it is that someone might say: suppose He is Lord, one who nurtures and is generous, yet He is not capable of all things. He answered this by saying He is Mighty, that is, capable of all possibilities, so He overcomes all and nothing overcomes Him.

The third: His being Forgiving. The benefit of mentioning it is that someone might say: suppose He is Lord and Benefactor, but He is such only toward the obedient who are sincere in worship. He answered this by saying that whoever remains in disbelief for seventy years and then repents, I remove his name from the register of the sinners, cover all his sins for him by My grace and mercy, and bring him to the ranks of the righteous.

Know that when He, exalted is He, made this clear, He said: ﴿Say: It is a great tidings.﴾ ﴿You are turning away from it.﴾ This great tidings may bear several meanings. It is possible that what is meant is that the saying that God is one is a great tidings; it is possible to say that what is meant is that the saying of prophethood is a great tidings; and it is possible to say that what is meant is that the affirmation of the gathering, the raising and the Resurrection is a great tidings. This is because these three matters were mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and for their sake the discourse extended to everything that preceded its mention. It is also possible that what is meant is the Qur'an being a miracle, because this too was mentioned earlier in His saying: ﴿A blessed Book, which We have revealed to you, that they may ponder its verses﴾ [Sad: 29], and these peoples turned away from it, as He said: ﴿Say: It is a great tidings. You are turning away from it.﴾ Know that His saying ﴿You are turning away from it﴾ is an encouragement to reflection and inference and a prohibition of blind imitation, because these matters are noble and lofty matters; for if a person is right regarding them he attains the greatest doors of happiness, and if he is wrong regarding them he falls into the greatest doors of misery. Thus these inquiries are great tidings and lofty, splendid matters, and plain reason obligates a person to exercise complete caution regarding them, and not to be content with laxity and leniency.

As for His exalted saying: ﴿I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly when they disputed﴾, know that He, exalted is He, encouraged the responsible to exercise caution in these four matters, and exaggerated that encouragement in several ways:

The first: that each of them is a great tidings, and a great tidings requires caution regarding it.

The second: that the exalted assembly disputed. The best that has been said about it is that when He, exalted is He, said:

صفحة ١٩٧
﴿I am placing on the earth a successor. They said: Will You place in it one who causes corruption in it and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You? He said: Indeed I know what you do not know﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 30]. The meaning is that they said: what benefit is there in creating mankind, since they occupy themselves with satisfying desire, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿one who causes corruption in it﴾, and with carrying out anger, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise﴾. Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed I know what you do not know.﴾ The statement of this answer, and Allah knows best, is that created beings, by rational division, are of four kinds:

One: those in whom intellect and wisdom are present, and in whom the soul and desire are not present, namely the angels alone.

Second: those in whom the soul and desire are present, and in whom knowledge and wisdom are not present, namely the beasts.

Third: things empty of both categories, namely inanimate objects.

There remains in the division a fourth kind (in which both matters are present), namely man. The purpose of creating man is not ignorance, blind imitation, arrogance and rebellion, for all of these are attributes of beasts and predators; rather, the purpose of his creation is the manifestation of knowledge, wisdom and obedience. So His saying ﴿Indeed I know what you do not know﴾ means that this kind of created being, although desire that calls to corruption and anger that drives it to shedding blood are present in it, yet intellect is present in it which calls it to knowledge, love, obedience and service. Since it is established that Allah, exalted is He, answered the angels with this answer, it is obligatory upon man to strive to attain these attributes, to exert effort in acquiring them, and to guard against the way of ignorance, blind imitation, persistence and arrogance. Since this is so, whoever comes to understand the manner of this event, his understanding of it becomes a call to him to diligence and striving in acquiring true knowledge and noble character, and a restraint from their opposites and contraries. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, mentioned this discourse in this place.

If it is said: the angels cannot be said to have disputed because of their saying ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption in it and sheds blood?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 30], for disputing with Allah is disbelief. We say: there is no doubt that a question and answer took place there, and that resembles disputation and debate, and resemblance is a cause for the permissibility of metaphor. For this reason the use of the word "disputation" for it is appropriate. When Allah, exalted is He, commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) to mention this discourse by way of symbolism, He commanded him to say: ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner.﴾ That is: I did not know of this disputation except through revelation, and Allah revealed this story to me only so that I may warn you by it, and so that this story may move you to sincerity in obedience and to guard against ignorance and blind imitation.

Since it is established that Allah, exalted is He, answered the angels with this answer, it is obligatory upon man to strive to attain these attributes, to exert effort in acquiring them, and to guard against the way of ignorance, blind imitation, persistence and arrogance. Since this is so, whoever comes to understand the manner of this event, his understanding of it becomes a call to him to diligence and striving in acquiring true knowledge and noble character, and a restraint from their opposites and contraries. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, mentioned this discourse in this place.

If it is said: the angels cannot be said to have disputed because of their saying ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption in it and sheds blood?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 30], for disputing with Allah is disbelief. We say: there is no doubt that a question and answer took place there, and that resembles disputation and debate, and resemblance is a cause for the permissibility of metaphor. For this reason the use of the word "disputation" for it is appropriate. When Allah, exalted is He, commanded Muhammad (ﷺ) to mention this discourse by way of symbolism, He commanded him to say: ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am a plain warner.﴾ That is: I did not know of this disputation except through revelation, and Allah revealed this story to me only so that I may warn you by it, and so that this story may move you to sincerity in obedience and to guard against ignorance and blind imitation.

[Page 198]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am creating a human from clay."﴾ ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration.﴾ ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely.﴾ ﴿Except Iblis; he was arrogant and was among the disbelievers.﴾ ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My two hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?"﴾ ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are expelled.﴾ ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are of those reprieved﴾ ﴿until the Day of the appointed time."﴾ ﴿He said, "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾ ﴿except Your chosen servants among them."﴾ ﴿He said, "The truth, and the truth I say:﴾ ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you among them, all together."﴾

Know that the purpose of mentioning this story is to forbid envy and arrogance. This is because Iblis fell into what he fell into only on account of envy and arrogance, and the disbelievers opposed Muhammad, peace be upon him, only on account of envy and arrogance. So God, exalted is He, mentioned this story here so that hearing it would deter them from these two blameworthy traits. The summary is that He, exalted is He, encouraged the responsible persons to reflect and to reason, and prohibited them from persistence and blind imitation (taqlid). In establishing this, He mentioned four matters.

The first of them: it is a great report, so caution must be exercised regarding it.

The second: the story of the angels' question about the wisdom in creating humans shows that the original wisdom in creating Adam is knowledge and obedience, not ignorance and arrogance.

The third: Iblis disputed with Adam, peace be upon him, only for the sake of envy and arrogance, so the rational person must guard against both. This is the coherence (nazm) of these verses. Know that this story has already been explained in many surahs, so there is no benefit in repeating it except for what is necessary. In it there are issues:

The first issue: regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human from clay.﴾ There are objections:

The first: this phrasing would be correct only if it were possible to create a human not from clay, just as if one said, "I am making a bracelet of gold," which is valid only if it were possible to make it from silver.

The second: here He mentioned that He created the human from clay, while in other verses He mentioned that He created him from other things, such as His saying regarding Adam that He created him from dust, and His saying: ﴿from dry clay, from black mud altered﴾ [al-Hijr: 28], and His saying: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾ [al-Anbiya': 37].

The third: this verse indicates that when He informed the angels that He was creating a human from clay, they said nothing. But in the other verse, where He said: ﴿Indeed, I am making upon the earth a successive authority﴾, He showed that they raised a question and an answer, and between them there is a contradiction.

As for the answer to the first objection: the meaning is as if He, glory be to Him, first described to them that the human is a person combining the bestial power, the predatory power, the satanic power, and the angelic power. So when He said: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human from clay,﴾ it is as if He said: that person, combining those qualities, I am creating him only from clay.

As for the answer to the second: the remote material is dust, nearer to it is clay, nearer to it is black mud altered, and nearer to it is dry clay. Thus it is established that there is no contradiction among them all.

As for the answer to the third: in the verse mentioned in the Surah of al-Baqarah, He informed them that He would create a successor on the earth, and in the verse mentioned here He showed that this successor is a human created from clay.

The second issue: He said: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit﴾. This indicates that the creation of the human is not complete except by two matters: first the proportioning (taswiyah), then the breathing of the spirit second. This is true, because the human is composed of a body and a soul.

[Page 199]

As for the body: it is produced only from semen, and semen is produced only from menstrual blood, and that in turn is produced only from the four humors, and they are produced only from the four elements. In achieving this proportioning, there must be the observance of a specific quantity for each of them, the observance of the manner of their mixing and compositions, and the observance of the period in which that temperament (mizaj) is attained, by which readiness arises to receive the rational soul (al-nafs al-nathiqah).

As for the soul: the reference to it is in His saying: ﴿and I breathed into him of My spirit.﴾ Since He attributed the spirit to Himself, this indicates that it is a noble, lofty, holy substance. The Incarnationists (al-hulūliyyah, those who hold God indwells creatures) went to the view that the word "min" (of) indicates partition, and this suggests that the spirit is a part of the parts of God, exalted is He. This is extreme corruption, because whatever has a part and a whole is composite, contingent in its existence, and originated.

As for the manner of breathing the spirit: know that the closest view is that the substance of the soul is a reference to transparent luminous bodies, of celestial element and holy substance, which permeate the body as light permeates the air and as fire permeates coal. This much is known. As for the manner of that breathing, it is among the matters that none knows except God, exalted is He.

The third issue: the fā' (then) in His saying: ﴿fa-qa'ū lahu sājidīn (then fall down before him in prostration)﴾ indicates that as soon as the breathing of the spirit into the body was complete, God's command to them to prostrate was directed at them. As for whether those commanded to this prostration were the angels of the earth, or whether the angels of the heavens entered into it, such as Jibril and Mikail, and the Greatest Spirit mentioned in His saying: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in ranks﴾ [al-Naba': 38], there are profound discussions regarding it. Some of the Sufis said: the angels who were commanded to prostrate to Adam are the vegetative powers and the sensory and motive animal powers, for in the human body they are the servants of the rational soul. Iblis, who did not prostrate, is the estimative faculty (al-quwwah al-wahmiyyah), which contends against the essence of the intellect. The discussion on this is lengthy. As for the remaining issues: the manner of the angels' prostration to Adam; whether that indicates his superiority over the angels or not; whether Iblis was among the angels or not; and whether he was an original disbeliever or not, all of this has been discussed in the Surah of al-Baqarah and elsewhere.

If it is the first, it follows that he must affirm a form to which nothing can be added in ugliness. For he must affirm a face such that nothing exists of it except a mere patch of face, based on His words, ﴿Everything perishes except His face﴾ [al-Qasas 28:88]. He must also affirm many eyes in that patch, based on His words, ﴿sailing under Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar 54:14]; and he must affirm one side, based on His words, ﴿O my regret over what I neglected concerning God's side﴾ [al-Zumar 39:56]; and he must affirm many hands upon that side, based on His words, ﴿of what Our hands have made﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:71]. And even if He has two hands, both must be on one side, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Black Stone is the right hand of God on earth." And he must affirm for Him one leg, based on His words, ﴿On the Day when a shin is laid bare﴾ [al-Qalam 68:42]. Thus what results from this form is merely a patch of face, with many eyes upon it, one side, many hands upon it, and one leg.

It is known that this form is the ugliest of forms. If this were a slave, no one would desire to buy him. How, then, can any rational person say that the Lord of the worlds is described by this form?

As for the second division: that he does not confine himself to the organs mentioned in the Qur'an, but adds to them or subtracts from them according to interpretations. In that case, his doctrine of taking the texts merely in their apparent sense is nullified, and he must accept the proofs of reason.

**The second argument:** against their claim that, if they affirm organs for God, then if they affirm for Him the male organ He is a male, and if they affirm for Him the female organ He is a female, and if they deny both, He is a eunuch or impotent. "Exalted is God above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation."

**The third argument:** that He, glorified and exalted is He, in His essence, either is a solid body that never bends at all, and thus is a solid rock, or He is capable of bending, and thus is soft, capable of being split and torn apart. "Exalted is God above that."

**The fourth argument:** that if He is such that He cannot move from His place, He is like a paralyzed, helpless invalid; and if He is such that He can move from His place, He is a locus of changes, and so falls under His words, ﴿I do not love those that set﴾ [al-An'am 6:76].

**The fifth argument:** if He does not eat, drink, sleep, or move, He is like a corpse; and if He does these things, He is a human being, highly prone to accusation, in need of eating, drinking, and intercourse. And this is false.

**The sixth argument:** they say that He descends every night from the Throne to the lowest heaven. We say to them, when He descends: does He remain managing the Throne while also managing the lowest heaven while He is on the Throne? In that case, there is no benefit in the descent. And if He does not remain managing the Throne, then at His descent He becomes deposed from the divinity of the Throne and the heavens.

**The seventh argument:** they say that He, exalted is He, is greater than the Throne, and that the Throne has no comparison in its greatness to the Footstool, and so on in this order until it reaches the lowest heaven. If that is so, then the lowest heaven, compared to the greatness of God, is like a speck of dust compared to the sea. Then, when He descends, either it is said that the God becomes small enough to be contained by the lowest heaven, or it is said that the lowest heaven becomes greater than the Throne. And all of this is false.

**The eighth argument:** it is established that the world is a sphere. If it is "above" relative to one people, it is "below" relative to other peoples, and that is false. And if it is "above" relative to all, then He would be a body encompassing this world from all sides, and thus the God of the world, on this view, would be one of the celestial spheres.

**The ninth argument:** since the earth is a sphere and the heavens are spheres, every hour that is assumed is, for certain peoples among the inhabitants of the sphere of the earth, the third of the night. So if He descended from the Throne at the third of the night, He would necessarily remain descending from the Throne forever and would never return to the Throne at all.

**The tenth argument:** we have only refuted the divinity of the sun and the moon on account of three kinds of defects:

The first: that it is composed of parts and components.

The second: that it is limited and finite.

The third: that it is described as moving, resting, rising, and setting.

If the God of the anthropomorphists (*al-mushabbiha*, those who likened God to creation) is composed of organs and parts, He is composite. If He is on the Throne, He is limited and finite. And if He descends from the Throne and returns to it, He is described as moving and resting. If these three attributes are incompatible with divinity, it is obligatory to declare God exempt from all of them, and that refutes the doctrine of the anthropomorphists. And if they are not incompatible with divinity, then no one can then criticize the divinity of the sun and the moon.

**The eleventh argument:** His words, ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ [al-Ikhlas 112:1]. The word *ahad* (One) is an intensive form expressing extreme unity, and that contradicts His being composed of parts and components.

**The twelfth argument:** His words, ﴿God is the Rich, and you are the poor﴾ [Muhammad 47:38]. If He were composed of parts and components, He would be in need of them, and that would prevent Him from being absolutely self-sufficient.

By these considerations it is established that the claim of affirming organs and parts for God is impossible. And since it has been established by certain proofs that God, exalted is He, must be declared exempt from these organs, we say: the scholars have mentioned several meanings for the word *yad* (hand):

The first: that *yad* is an expression for power. The Arabs say: "I have no *yad* (power) in this matter," meaning: no strength or capacity. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the bond of marriage should pardon﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:237].

The second: *yad* is an expression for blessing. It is said: "the *ayadi* (favors) of so-and-so toward so-and-so are manifest," and what is meant is blessings. And what is meant by "two hands" is the manifest and hidden blessings, or the blessings of religion and of the world.

The third: the word *yad* may be added for emphasis, as when someone says to one who has sinned with his tongue: "This is what your two hands have earned," and as in His words, ﴿glad tidings before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf 7:57].

The first: the apparent sense of the verse requires affirming two hands. So if *yad* were an expression for power, it would necessarily follow that God has two powers, and that is false.

The second: the verse indicates that Adam's being created with two hands is what necessitates his excellence and his being prostrated to by the angels. So if *yad* were an expression for power, Adam would have been created by power. But all things are created by the power of God, exalted is He. Therefore, just as Adam, peace be upon him, was created by the hand of God, exalted is He, so too Iblis was created by the hand of God, exalted is He. And on the assumption that it is an expression for power, this would not be a valid reason for Adam's being prostrated to over Iblis, and it would be no more fitting that Adam should be prostrated to Iblis than that Iblis should be prostrated to Adam. This is the limit of the discussion on this topic.

First: The celestial bodies are more noble than the elemental bodies. Fire is the element closest to the celestial sphere, and earth is the farthest from it. Therefore fire must be superior to earth.

Second: Fire is the substitute for the sun and the moon in illuminating this world when they are absent. The sun and the moon are more noble than earth, so their substitute in giving light is superior to earth.

Third: The primary active quality is either heat or cold, and heat is superior to cold, because heat suits life and cold suits death.

Fourth: Earth is dense and fire is subtle, and subtlety is more noble than density.

Fifth: Fire is luminous and earth is dark, and light is better than darkness.

As for the fact that whatever is more earthly and dusty is baser, the matter is evident.

Twelfth: Ripening, digestion and life are not completed except by heat, and were it not for the power of heat, the temperament would not be completed and compounds would not be generated.

Thirteenth: The strongest of the four elements in the power of acting is fire, and the most perfect of them in the power of being acted upon is earth, and acting is superior to being acted upon. Therefore fire is superior to earth.

Third: Earth dominates fire, for it extinguishes fire, whereas fire does not affect pure earth.

As for the Third Premise: it is that whoever's origin is better than the origin of another is better than him. If someone says: Suppose Iblis erred in this syllogism, how did disbelief necessarily follow for him from that opposition? The explanation of this question has several aspects:

First: His words, "Prostrate," are a command, and a command does not necessarily imply obligation but rather recommendation, and opposing a recommendation does not entail disobedience, let alone disbelief. Moreover, those who say that a command implies obligation do not deny that it admits recommendation with clear probability, and with the presence of this clear probability, how does disobedience follow, let alone disbelief?

Second: Suppose it implies obligation, yet Iblis was not one of the angels, and the command to the angels to prostrate to Adam does not include Iblis.

Third: Suppose it includes him, yet specifying the general by analogy is permissible, so he exempted himself from the generality of that command by analogy.

Fourth: Suppose he did not prostrate while knowing that he was commanded to do so, yet this degree entails disobedience and does not entail disbelief. How then did disbelief necessarily follow?

The answer: Suppose the form of a command does not indicate obligation, it is still possible that there be combined with it indications that show obligation, and here those indications were present, namely His words, ﴿Have you grown arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ So when Iblis brought his corrupt analogy, this indicated that he mentioned that analogy only so as to use it as a means to discredit the command of God and His commandment, and that entails disbelief.

Know that it is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that mentioning a ruling immediately after a fitting attribute indicates that the ruling is caused by that attribute. This indicates that specifying a text by analogy entails this ruling.

His words, ﴿from it﴾, meaning: from the Garden or from the heavens. "Rajim" means "stoned" (al-marjum), and concerning it there are two views:

The first: It is a metaphor for expulsion, because it is apparent that whoever is expelled may be pelted with stones, which is stoning. Since stoning is a necessary consequence of expulsion, stoning is used as a metonymy for expulsion. First: We take stoning as expulsion from the Garden or from the heavens, and we take cursing as expulsion from the mercy of God.

Second: We take stoning as expulsion, and we take His words ﴿and indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment﴾ as meaning that this expulsion extends to the end of the Resurrection, so this is an additional benefit and not a repetition.

The second view regarding the meaning of "rajim" is to take it literally, namely that the devils are stoned with meteors. And God knows best.

Third: The primary active quality is either heat or cold, and heat is superior to cold, because heat suits life and cold suits death.

Fourth: Earth is dense and fire is subtle, and subtlety is more noble than density.

Fifth: Fire is luminous and earth is dark, and light is better than darkness.

Sixth: Fire is light, resembling the spirit, and earth is heavy, resembling the body, and the spirit is superior to the body. Therefore fire is superior to earth. For this reason the physicians have agreed that the two heavy elements help in the composition of bodies, while the two light elements help in the generation of spirits.

Seventh: Fire rises and earth falls, and what rises is superior to what falls.

Eighth: The first of the zodiacal signs of the sphere is Aries, because it is the one that begins from the point of the northern equinox. Aries is of the nature of fire. The noblest organs of the living creature are the heart and the spirit, and both are of the nature of fire. The basest organ of the living creature is the bone, which is cold, dry and earthly.

Ninth: Earthly bodies, the more luminous they are and the more they resemble fire, the more noble they are, and the more they are dusty, dense, turbid and resembling earth, the baser they are. An example: bodies that resemble fire, such as gold, ruby, and pure luminous stones. Another example among garments is silk and what is made from it. As for the fact that whatever is more earthly and dusty is baser, the matter is evident.

Tenth: The faculty of sight is a faculty of the utmost nobility and majesty, and its action is not completed except by means of the ray, which is a body resembling fire.

Eleventh: The noblest body in the material world is the sun, and there is no doubt that it resembles fire in its form, its nature and its effect.

Twelfth: Ripening, digestion and life are not completed except by heat, and were it not for the power of heat, the temperament would not be completed and compounds would not be generated.

The first issue: Ḥafṣ... rather, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read ﴿fa-al-ḥaqqu﴾ with a nominative (raf') and ﴿wa-al-ḥaqqa﴾ with an accusative (naṣb), while the rest read both with the accusative. As for the nominative, its implied construction is: "So the truth is My oath." As for the accusative, it is governed by the sense of an oath, meaning: "By the truth," like your saying: "By God, I will surely do it." As for His words ﴿and the truth I say﴾, the word "al-ḥaqqa" is governed by the verb ﴿I say﴾.

The second issue: His words ﴿from you﴾ mean: from your kind, namely the devils. ﴿And whoever follows you from among them﴾ refers to the descendants of Adam. If it is asked: The word ﴿all together﴾ is an emphasis of what? We say: It may be an emphasis of the pronoun in ﴿from them﴾, or of the pronoun "you" in ﴿from you﴾ together with ﴿whoever follows you﴾, and its meaning: I will surely fill Hell with both the leaders and the followers, leaving none of them behind.

The third issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued with this verse on the question that everything is by the decree of God, in several aspects:

First: He, Exalted is He, said concerning Iblis: ﴿Then get out of it, for you are accursed﴾, and ﴿and indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment﴾. This is a report from God, Exalted is He, that he will not believe. So if he were to believe, the true report of God would turn into a lie, which is impossible. Therefore the proceeding of faith from him was impossible, even though he was commanded to it.

Second: He said: ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all﴾. God, Exalted is He, knew that he would mislead them, and heard from him this claim, and He was able to prevent him from that. And one who is able to prevent but does not prevent is pleased with it. If they say: Perhaps that prevention would be corrupting, we say: This is a corrupt statement, because that prevention would deliver Iblis from misleading and deliver the children of Adam from going astray, and this is the very essence of benefit.

Third: He, Exalted is He, informed that He will fill Hell with the disbelievers. So if they did not disbelieve, falsehood and ignorance would follow with regard to God, Exalted is He.

Fourth: If He had willed that the disbeliever not disbelieve, it would be necessary that He preserve the prophets and the righteous and cause Iblis and the devils to die. Since He reversed the matter, we know that this is corrupt.

The fifth point: the obligation placed on those disbelievers to have faith requires that they be obligated to believe these verses, which indicate that they will absolutely not believe. In that case, it would follow that they become obligated to believe that they will absolutely not believe, and that is an obligation to do what cannot be borne. And God knows best.

[Page 200 continues from the preceding section]

The First Premise: Iblis was created from fire. This is indicated by his words, quoted from him, ﴿You created me from fire, and created him from clay﴾, and by the words of God, Exalted is He, ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of scorching wind﴾ [al-Hijr 15:27].

The Second Premise: Fire is superior to clay. This is indicated by several arguments:

First: The celestial bodies are more noble than the elemental bodies. Fire is the element closest to the celestial sphere, and earth is the farthest from it. Therefore fire must be superior to earth.

Second: Fire is the substitute for the sun and the moon in illuminating this world when they are absent. The sun and the moon are more noble than earth, so their substitute in giving light is superior to earth.

Third: The primary active quality is either heat or cold, and heat is superior to cold, because heat suits life and cold suits death.

Fourth: Earth is dense and fire is subtle, and subtlety is more noble than density.

Fifth: Fire is luminous and earth is dark, and light is better than darkness.

Sixth: Fire is light, resembling the spirit, and earth is heavy, resembling the body, and the spirit is superior to the body. Therefore fire is superior to earth. For this reason the physicians have agreed that the two heavy elements help in the composition of bodies, while the two light elements help in the generation of spirits.

Seventh: Fire rises and earth falls, and what rises is superior to what falls.

Eighth: The first of the zodiacal signs of the sphere is Aries, because it is the one that begins from the point of the northern equinox. Aries is of the nature of fire. The noblest organs of the living creature are the heart and the spirit, and both are of the nature of fire. The basest organ of the living creature is the bone, which is cold, dry and earthly.

Ninth: Earthly bodies, the more luminous they are and the more they resemble fire, the more noble they are, and the more they are dusty, dense, turbid and resembling earth, the baser they are. An example: bodies that resemble fire, such as gold, ruby, and pure luminous stones. Another example among garments is silk and what is made from it. As for the fact that whatever is more earthly and dusty is baser, the matter is evident.

Tenth: The faculty of sight is a faculty of the utmost nobility and majesty, and its action is not completed except by means of the ray, which is a body resembling fire.

Eleventh: The noblest body in the material world is the sun, and there is no doubt that it resembles fire in its form, its nature and its effect.

Twelfth: Ripening, digestion and life are not completed except by heat, and were it not for the power of heat, the temperament would not be completed and compounds would not be generated.

Thirteenth: The strongest of the four elements in the power of acting is fire, and the most perfect of them in the power of being acted upon is earth, and acting is superior to being acted upon. Therefore fire is superior to earth.

As for those who hold that earth is superior to fire, they also mentioned arguments:

First: Earth is a trustworthy reformer. If you deposit a seed with it, it returns to you as a fruit-bearing tree, whereas fire is a traitor that corrupts everything you entrust to it.

Second: The sense of sight praised fire, so let him listen to what the sense of touch says.

Third: Earth dominates fire, for it extinguishes fire, whereas fire does not affect pure earth.

As for the Third Premise: it is that whoever's origin is better than the origin of another is better than him. Know that this premise is extremely false, because the origin of ashes is fire, while the origin of pleasant gardens and fruit-bearing trees is clay, and it is known by necessity that fruit-bearing trees are better than ashes. Moreover, suppose that considering this aspect entails excellence, it can still be countered by another aspect that entails preponderance. Take a man of noble lineage who is devoid of all virtues: his lineage makes him preferred, yet one who is not of noble lineage may be abundant in knowledge and asceticism, and so he is better than that man of lineage by degrees without limit. Thus the false premise in the syllogism that Iblis mentioned is this premise.

If someone says: Suppose Iblis erred in this syllogism, how did disbelief necessarily follow for him from that opposition? The explanation of this question has several aspects:

First: His words, "Prostrate," are a command, and a command does not necessarily imply obligation but rather recommendation, and opposing a recommendation does not entail disobedience, let alone disbelief. Moreover, those who say that a command implies obligation do not deny that it admits recommendation with clear probability, and with the presence of this clear probability, how does disobedience follow, let alone disbelief?

Second: Suppose it implies obligation, yet Iblis was not one of the angels, and the command to the angels to prostrate to Adam does not include Iblis.

Third: Suppose it includes him, yet specifying the general by analogy is permissible, so he exempted himself from the generality of that command by analogy.

Fourth: Suppose he did not prostrate while knowing that he was commanded to do so, yet this degree entails disobedience and does not entail disbelief. How then did disbelief necessarily follow?

The answer: Suppose the form of a command does not indicate obligation, it is still possible that there be combined with it indications that show obligation, and here those indications were present, namely His words, ﴿Have you grown arrogant, or were you among the exalted?﴾ So when Iblis brought his corrupt analogy, this indicated that he mentioned that analogy only so as to use it as a means to discredit the command of God and His commandment, and that entails disbelief.

Having understood this, we say: When Iblis mentioned this corrupt analogy, God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Then get out of it, for you are accursed﴾.

Know that it is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that mentioning a ruling immediately after a fitting attribute indicates that the ruling is caused by that attribute. Here, the ruling that he is "accursed" (rajim) came immediately after what was related about him, that he specified a text by analogy. This indicates that specifying a text by analogy entails this ruling.

His words, ﴿from it﴾, meaning: from the Garden or from the heavens. "Rajim" means "stoned" (al-marjum), and concerning it there are two views:

The first: It is a metaphor for expulsion, because it is apparent that whoever is expelled may be pelted with stones, which is stoning. Since stoning is a necessary consequence of expulsion, stoning is used as a metonymy for expulsion. If they say: expulsion is cursing, then if we take His words "rajim" to mean expulsion, His words after that, ﴿and indeed upon you is My curse﴾, would be a repetition. The answer has two aspects:

First: We take stoning as expulsion from the Garden or from the heavens, and we take cursing as expulsion from the mercy of God.

Second: We take stoning as expulsion, and we take His words ﴿and indeed upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment﴾ as meaning that this expulsion extends to the end of the Resurrection, so this is an additional benefit and not a repetition.

The second view regarding the meaning of "rajim" is to take it literally, namely that the devils are stoned with meteors. And God knows best.

If it is said: The word "ilā" (until) indicates the end of a span, so His words ﴿until the Day of Judgment﴾ require that this curse ends when the Day of Judgment comes. The author of al-Kashshaf answered that the curse remains upon him in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, kinds of punishment will be added to the curse, so that the curse, with the presence of those punishments, becomes forgotten.

Know that when Iblis became accursed, he said: ﴿Then grant me respite until the day they are resurrected﴾. It was said: He only asked for respite until the day of resurrection in order to escape death, for if he were granted respite until the day of resurrection, he would not die before the day of resurrection, and when the day of resurrection comes, he will not die either, and so he would escape death. Then God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So you are among the ones granted respite﴾, ﴿until the day of the appointed time﴾. Its meaning: You are among those granted respite until a day that God knows and no one other than Him knows. Then Iblis said: ﴿By Your might﴾, an oath by the might of God and His authority, ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾. Here he attributed the misleading to himself, which is the view of the Qadariyya (those who affirm human free will), and he said on another occasion: ﴿My Lord, because You have led me astray﴾, attributing the misleading to God, in accordance with the view of the Jabriyya (determinists). This indicates that he is confused on this issue.

* * *

As for His words, ﴿except Your sincere servants from among them﴾, there are several benefits:

The first benefit: It was said: Iblis's purpose in mentioning this exception was that no falsehood should occur in his speech, for if he had not mentioned this exception and claimed that he would mislead everyone, his lie would have become evident when he failed to mislead the righteous servants of God. It is as if Iblis said: I only mentioned this exception so that falsehood would not occur in this speech. And for this reason it is said: lying is something Iblis disdains, so how is it fitting for a Muslim to engage in it? If it is said: How is this verse reconciled with His words: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan cast into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj 22:52]? We say: Iblis did not say, "I did not intend to mislead the righteous servants of God." Rather he said, "I will surely mislead them," and although he intends to mislead, he does not actually mislead them.

The second benefit: This verse indicates that Iblis does not mislead the sincere servants of God. And God, Exalted is He, said concerning Joseph: ﴿Indeed he is among Our sincere servants﴾ [Yusuf 12:24]. From the combination of these two verses we conclude that Iblis did not mislead Joseph, peace be upon him, and this indicates the falsehood of the Hashwiyya (literalist traditionalists) in what they attribute to Joseph, peace be upon him, of vile acts.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 38, verses 86–88:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it, nor am I of those who pretend.﴾ ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while.﴾

Know that Allah, exalted is He, concluded this surah with this noble conclusion, because He, exalted is He, mentioned many proofs indicating the obligation of exercising caution in seeking the religion. Then He said at the conclusion: this is what I call people to, and it must be examined in the state of the one calling and in the state of the call itself, so that it becomes clear whether it is truth or falsehood. As for the caller, who is I, I do not ask you for any wage or wealth for this call. It is evident that the liar's greed for wealth never ceases at all, and it was evident that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was far from worldly things and had no desire for them. As for the manner of the call, He said: "nor am I of those who pretend." The exegetes have mentioned several meanings for it, and what most strongly prevails in my estimation is that the intended meaning is that this which I call you to is a religion that does not need, in knowing its soundness, many artificial efforts, but rather is a religion whose soundness is attested by the plain intellect. For I call you, first, to acknowledge the existence of Allah; second, I call you to declare Him free of and sanctified above everything unbefitting to Him, strengthened by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11] and similar verses; third, I call you to acknowledge that He is described with perfection of knowledge, power, wisdom and mercy; fourth, I call you to acknowledge that He is exempt from partners and opposites; fifth, I call you to refrain from worshipping these idols, which are base inanimate objects, there being no benefit in worshipping them nor harm in turning away from them; sixth, I call you to honour the pure and sanctified spirits, namely the angels and the prophets; seventh, I call you to acknowledge resurrection and the Last Day: ﴿That He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [al-Najm: 31]; eighth, I call you to turn away from this world and turn toward the Hereafter. These eight principles are the strong and recognized principles in the religion of Allah, exalted is He, and the religion of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and in the beginning of intellects, and the first of thoughts bears witness to the soundness of these eight principles. Thus it is established that I am not of those who pretend in the Sharia to which I call the creation; rather, every sound intellect and upright disposition bears witness to its soundness, its majesty, and its distance from falsehood and corruption, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.﴾ When He had explained these premises, He said: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while.﴾ The meaning is: if you persist in ignorance and blind imitation, and refuse to accept these clarifications we have mentioned, then after a while you will know whether you were right or wrong in this turning away. Mentioning such a statement after those preceding clarifications is something to which nothing can be added in terms of warning and intimidation. And Allah knows best.

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The tafsir of this surah was completed on Thursday, at the end of Tuesday, the second of the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah, in the year six hundred and three. Praise be to Allah for His bounties, and blessings upon His purified servants on earth and in heaven, and praise and commendation as befits His attributes and names, and complete veneration for His prophets and saints, and peace upon them in abundance until the Day of Judgment.
